A classic example of a drug-nutrient interaction resulting in 
harmful side eﬀ ects is the interaction between pressor agents
in foods (tyramine, dopamine, histamine, phenylethylamine)
and monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors (e.g., Nardil). Th is 
interaction can result in sudden increases in blood pressure 
with resulting complications. Box 11.2 outlines the speciﬁ cs for
this drug-nutrient interaction.
